text:
pagerduty-bot: Incident PAGER: high 5xx rate observed for ingress in eu-west-2 (eastus3-equivalent) — paging on-call network (oncall-net)

sanjay: I see p50 ok but p99 latency and 502/504 spike starting ~09:12 UTC. Grafana: spike across ALB fronting ingress.

irina: Confirming from logs: Envoy downstream reset count up ~8x. Also a bunch of 502s from nginx ingress controller.

melissa: Customer-impact: support dashboard shows ~2.3% of requests failing for a subset of customers in eu-west-2. CS reported errors from real-time features.

luca: I'm on it — grabbing target health from ALB and pod status.

luca: ```
# aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:... | jq '.TargetHealthDescriptions[] | {Id:.Target.Id, State:.TargetHealth.State, Reason:.TargetHealth.Description}'
```

luca: target states look mostly healthy but a few targets in azb show `draining` then `healthy` oscillation.

kai: Route53 records for the service have 300s TTL. We recently changed weighted routing policies last week. Could be propagation wobble.

irina: Also seeing a flurry of TCP conn resets on NLB-to-envoy from host-level conntrack logs in azb. kernel logs show conntrack prune spikes.

melissa: Pager: note customer-facing comms queued. We need an ETA & mitigation before 30min.

sanjay: Quick mitigation plan: 1) Reduce DNS TTL to 30s for affected record 2) Shift weight to backup region (euc2) via weighted Route53 3) Scale up ingress pods in azb and increase ALB target-group healthy threshold 4) Temp enable ALB connection_draining 5) Investigate conntrack limits on nodes

luca: Doing step 1 & 2 now. Changing TTL and shifting 35% traffic to euc2.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Route53 change request: set TTL=30 for service.example.com — change-id Z3XYZ — status: PENDING

kai: I'll monitor propagation. Also checking if our loadbalancer healthcheck interval is too aggressive causing flaps.

irina: Ran `kubectl get pods -n ingress -o wide` — nodes in azb show higher pod restart counts and netdev rx errors on eth0.

luca: Scaling ingress replica count +2 in azb nodepool: ```kubectl scale deployment ingress --replicas=6 -n ingress```

sanjay: Ops note: conntrack exhaustion will show as `nf_conntrack: table full` in dmesg. If we hit that again, we'll bump net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max and roll kernel params via sysctl daemonset.

support-jen: Support update: some customers on real-time APIs still seeing 5xx after initial shift. Sending targeted retry guidance to SDK teams.

melissa: We're drafting a short status update: "Investigating increased 5xx in eu-west-2. Traffic being shifted to a secondary region; mitigation in progress." Send once we confirm improved metrics.

luca: ALB target-group deregister events show a pattern: targets get marked unhealthy, then healthy within ~20s repeatedly. Healthcheck threshold is 2 failures -> unhealthy. Lowering sensitivity to 5 failures and increasing interval.

irina: Command used: ```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --attributes Key=slow_start.duration_seconds,Value=30
```

luca: Also increased health check healthy threshold to 5 and interval to 20s. Hoping to stop flapping.

kai: Route53 change applied: weight adjusted: primary 65%, backup 35%. TTL now 30s. Change propagated to 8/12 resolvers so far.

sanjay: Stack-level mitigations: enabled ALB connection_draining with 300s, increased target-group deregistration delay. This should allow in-flight requests to drain and reduce 502 churn.

ops-bot: monitoring: ALB 5xx rate decreasing from 2.3% -> 1.1% after weight shift. Envoy reset count down ~45% in azb.

melissa: Good. Prepare handoff: on-call networking before shift stabilizes and we finish root cause.

irina: Root cause hypothesis: simultaneous conntrack pruning + aggressive healthcheck caused targets to flapping in azb; combined with Route53 weighted changes some clients hit cold route propagation leading to bursts on a subset of targets -> overload -> conn reset -> 502s. Need postmortem to confirm.

luca: I'll collect packet captures from an affected node and ALB logs for the incident window.

sanjay: Handoff to @kai (network oncall) for mitigation follow-through and RCA coordination. @irina will own data collection & initial RCA. @melissa will coordinate customer comms. @luca stays on triage for any rollback.

kai: Acknowledged. I'll keep monitoring Route53 and node conntrack metrics. If we see >0.5% 5xx again we'll consider shifting more traffic or emergency IP failover.

support-jen: CS will send interim note to impacted customers now.

melissa: Interim status posted: "Mitigation in progress: traffic partially shifted to backup region, ingress replicas scaled, LB health-check sensitivity tuned. Monitoring for improvement." :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: dashboard snapshot: 5xx now at 0.9%, p99 latency still elevated but trending down.

sanjay: Closing initial pager. Handing ongoing to network on-call. Please keep this thread updated with any regressions.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PAGER: acknowledged by kai — status: monitoring.

kai: Follow-ups: plan to (1) deploy conntrack-tuning daemonset with conservative raise to nf_conntrack_max (2) run soak tests on ingress in azb (3) schedule PM to audit Route53 weight automation to avoid simultaneous changes.

irina: Collecting logs + pcaps and will attach to postmortem ticket.

melissa: ETA for full RCA ticket and customer postmortem draft: EOD.

sanjay: Thanks all. If anyone sees new spike, @kai and @sanjay oncall escalate immediately.

kai: last note — we should add a runbook entry: "If ALB healthy state flaps + conntrack spikes -> reduce DNS TTL, shift weight, increase health thresholds, scale ingress, enable draining". I'll add PR after incident.

ops-bot: incident log appended to ticket INC-2026-1843.

melissa: marking handoff done, leaving channel.

kai: I'll update thread when RCA has more detail.

support-jen: closing support alert after customers ack transient errors resolved.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PAGER: resolved state set to MONITORING by kai at 09:28 UTC."
